retracted_claim: replacing the endpoint tangent with an arc is refuted
why_wrong: The held-out anchors used as the reference are produced by the sequential rail tracker, whose candidate score is support / (1 + 4*|center - expected| + ...) with expected being the straight-line extrapolation of the previous anchor. Far anchors are therefore pulled toward the tangent by the very mechanism that finds them, so scoring a straight model against a curved one on that reference favours the straight one by construction. The anchor bias was recorded on day one, but only as the weaker statement that the measured error is a lower bound; the directional consequence was missed.
alternative_hypothesis_tested_and_reject: That an unregularised quadratic fit was to blame. Repeating the comparison with curvature shrunk to zero below 4 standard errors over a 30 m window, matching the other branch, still shows the tangent ahead on curved frames of the extended recording: 0.172 m against 1.839 m at 20 m past the anchors. The implementation was not the cause; the reference was.

correct_measurement.source: docs/CURVED_CORRIDOR_AND_RANGE.md on branches buyanov and autoresearch
correct_measurement.method: pair test against what a later frame measures over the same ground at close range

still_standing: the extended recording contains real curves: their 21 per cent against our 22 per cent, measured independently
the six sourcecraft recordings carry no measurable curvature
path uncertainty is optimistic on curves
lesson: A reference generated by one of the models under comparison picks the winner for you.
